correctness.rationale: The full-trace witness puts all support points at distance two. If their mutual distance is four, the unique geodesic midpoint is the only witness containing that pair, and it cannot omit a third support point. Otherwise all pairs have distance two (even parity and distance at most four), and tree path uniqueness forces a single common neighbor u. For a support in N(u), u gives the empty trace; marked neighbors give the complements of themselves and unmarked neighbors give the full trace. A vertex at depth at least two from u can only see a marked neighbor in its own branch, and realizes that singleton exactly at depth three in that branch. These exhaust possible traces. They give the exact criterion for triples, rule out any two-point trace for a centered support of size at least four, and permit counting at the unique u with no multiplicity. The center, three marked and one unmarked neighbors, and two further vertices in each of three disjoint marked branches require at least eleven vertices. The explicit eleven-vertex tree gives all eight traces, including the complementary-pair witnesses inside the support. The structural proof applies to all tree sizes; no finite run is being used in its place.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Setting r=2 forces h=t=j=1 where j is the branching depth used for each singleton witness. A fourth component must have a depth-one vertex and each marked neighbor must have an outward path of length two. This is exactly degree at least four and the three outward-deep neighbors; 3r+5 gives eleven.
